Rashi on Chullin 67a:10:1.hebrew: דהאי הוא דמוכח אהאיך - קרא דיש לו, דלמשרי כלים אתא:
Rashi on Chullin 67a:10:1.english: That this [verse] proves [the meaning of] the other - [namely,] the verse of "that has [fins and scales]," that it comes to permit [fish in] vessels:

Rashi on Chullin 67a:10:2.hebrew: דאי מהאיך הוה אמינא - "בנחלים אותם תאכלו", הא בכלים אפי' אותם לא תאכלו; ואתא "בימים ובנחלים" דאין לו, וגלי עליה דכי מעטינהו לכלים, מאיסורא מעטינהו ולא מהיתרא:
Rashi on Chullin 67a:10:2.english: As, if from the other [verse], I would say - "In the rivers, those you may eat" — [implying that] in vessels, even those [with fins and scales] you may not eat; and [then the phrase] "in the seas and in the rivers" of [the verse] "that have not [fins and scales]" comes and reveals about it that when [Scripture] excluded vessels, it excluded them from the prohibition and not from the permission:

Rashi on Chullin 67a:11:1.hebrew: לשפי - לשון "השופה יין לחמרא" (ב"מ דף ס.), לשון מוריק מכלי אל כלי:
Rashi on Chullin 67a:11:1.english: Should [not] pour - [This is] the [same] expression [as] "one who pours wine into wine" (Bava Metzia 60a), [i.e.,] an expression of pouring from vessel to vessel:

Rashi on Chullin 67a:11:2.hebrew: שיכרא - של תמרים הוא, ומצויין בהן תולעים:
Rashi on Chullin 67a:11:2.english: Beer - It is [made] of dates, and worms are common in them:

Rashi on Chullin 67a:11:3.english: Through straw - [This refers to] twigs, as they strain it [the beer] through thin pieces of wood and straws:

Rashi on Chullin 67a:11:4.hebrew: באורתא - שאם תפול תולעת על הקשים, לא יראנה, ומשם תפול לכלי, ולמחר כשיראנה, יהא סבר שלא יצתה מן השכר לקשים, ותולעת המים מותרת כדאמרן:
Rashi on Chullin 67a:11:4.english: At night - For if a worm falls onto the straws, he will not see it, and from there it will fall into the vessel; and the next day, when he sees it, he will think that it did not emerge from the beer onto the straws, and a water worm is permitted, as we said [earlier]:

Rashi on Chullin 67a:11:5.hebrew: וקעבר משום שרץ השורץ על הארץ - דכיון דרחשה והלכה קצת על הקשין, נעשית שרץ הארץ:
Rashi on Chullin 67a:11:5.english: And he violates [the prohibition of] "a swarming thing that swarms upon the earth" - For since it crawled and went a bit on the straws, it becomes a swarming thing of the earth:

Rashi on Chullin 67a:13:1.english: That is its [normal manner of] growth - and it is as though it had not separated from the water:

Rashi on Chullin 67a:14:1.english: Yavḥushin [gnats] - A type of tiny gnats that are found in wine cellars:

Rashi on Chullin 67a:1:1.hebrew: הטל פרט - הסמוך להם, ותנהו ביניהם, ודונם בכלל ופרט וכלל, ותרבי ביה כל כעין הפרט. הלכך אי לאו "תאכלו" קמא, הוה מרבינן בכעין הפרט אפי' בורות, דדמו לפרט בהכי שהן מים גדלין על גבי קרקע; אבל השתא דכתיב "תאכלו" קמא, דרשינן ליה הכי: מה הפרט מפורש מים נובעין, אף כל מים נובעים — ואיתרבו חריצין ונעיצין לאיסורא כאלו, ולא איתרבו בורות:
Rashi on Chullin 67a:1:1.english: Place the detail - that is adjacent to them, and put it between them, and expound them as a generalization, and a detail, and a generalization, and [thereby] include everything similar to the detail. Therefore, were it not for the first [instance of] "you may eat," we would include as similar to the detail even cisterns, which resemble the detail in that they are waters that gather upon the ground; however, now that the first "you may eat" is written, we expound it thus: Just as the detail is explicitly springing waters, so too any springing waters [are included] — and [thus] ditches and trenches are included in the prohibition like these [seas and rivers], whereas cisterns are not included:

Rashi on Chullin 67a:2:1.english: And what does [it] include - through [the principle of] "similar to the detail" of "so too all":

Rashi on Chullin 67a:2:2.english: And what [does it] exclude? - For every detail comes to exclude [something]:

Rashi on Chullin 67a:3:1.hebrew: ואימא מה הפרט מפורש וכו' - דאע"ג דלא דמי ליה לפרטא אלא בחד צד, מרבינן, דכללא בתרא דוקא:
Rashi on Chullin 67a:3:1.english: And say: Just as the detail is explicit, etc. - For even though it is not similar to the detail except in one aspect, we include [it], because the final generalization is determinative.

Rashi on Chullin 67a:4:1.hebrew: א"כ תאכלו מאי אהני ליה - בלאו איהו נמי, כלים לא מיתסרי, דהא לא דמו לפרט במידי, אלא לאו "תאכלו" למשרי בורות אתא, ולמימרא דלא תרבי בכעין הפרט אלא חריצין ונעיצין דדמו ליה בשני צדדין:
Rashi on Chullin 67a:4:1.english: If so, what use is [the phrase] "may you eat" to it? - Even without it, [creatures in] vessels would not be forbidden, for they do not resemble the detail at all; rather, does "may you eat" not come to permit [those in] pits, and to say that you should not include as "similar to the detail" anything except trenches and water channels, which resemble it in two respects:

Rashi on Chullin 67a:4:3.hebrew: נעיצין - רחבין, כגון אותן שעושין לביברי דגים:
Rashi on Chullin 67a:4:3.english: Ne'itzin [water channels] - [These are] wide, such as those that are made for fishponds:

Rashi on Chullin 67a:4:4.hebrew: "ואימא איפכא" לא גרסינן הכא, עד בסיפא דשמעתא בתר מלתא דתנא דבי <abbr title="רבי">ר'</abbr> ישמעאל; אבל הכא גבי תנא דבי רב דדריש כללי ופרטי, ליכא לאותביה, דהא כעין הפרט בעינן, ומאי כעין הפרט אית בהו דתרבינהו לאיסורא ותפיק חריצין ונעיצין:
Rashi on Chullin 67a:4:4.english: We do not read [the text] "And say the opposite" here, [but rather] at the end of the passage, after the statement of the Tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael; however, here, with regard to the Tanna of the school of Rav, who expounds [using] generalizations and details, one cannot raise this objection, for we require [that the included items be] similar to the detail, and what similarity to the detail do they [i.e., pits, ditches, and caves] have, that you should include them for prohibition and exclude trenches and water channels?

Rashi on Chullin 67a:5:1.hebrew: במים במים ב' פעמים - הואיל ושני הכללות סמוכין, כשתטיל פרט שאחריהם ביניהם, מדה בתורה היא שלא תדונם בכלל ופרט אלא ברבוי ומיעוט, דלהכי פלגינהו רחמנא לפרטא מכללא, דלא תדרשיה בכלל ופרט: ואיכא בין ריבה ומיעט לכלל ופרט, דכי דרשינן כלל ופרט, הוי פרט פירושו של כללא, ואין בכלל אלא מה שבפרט, ואפי' דבר הדומה לו אין לך להביא; וכשכלל לך כלל שני אחר הפרט, אהני לאתויי מידי דדמי ליה לפרט: אבל כי דרשינן ריבה ומיעט, לא פירש המיעוט את הרבוי, אלא מיעט שלא תשמע ממנו הכל, אלא זה והדומים לו, ובלאו רבוי שני הוה מרבינן כל דדמי ליה למיעוטא; ואהני רבוי שני לאתויי כל מילי, ואהני מיעוטא למעוטי מידי דלא דמי ליה כלל; והכי מפרשינן בפ' נגמר הדין (סנהדרין דף מה:) גבי כל הנסקלין נתלין, דרבוי ומיעוט לחודיה מייתי כל דדמי ליה בכל מילי: ומשום דרבוי ומיעוט מידריש, איצטריך "תאכלו" קמא למשרי בורות, דאתי ברבוי ומיעוט וריבוי לאיסורא; דאילו בכלל ופרט דרשינן ליה, לא הוו מתרבו בורות, ולא איצטריך "תאכלו" יתירא, דקסבר תנא דבי ר' ישמעאל כללא קמא דוקא, דלא מרבי כללא בתרא אלא מידי דדמי לפרט בכל צד, דהיינו נובעין: וה"נ אמרן לעיל גבי כלל ופרט דחגבים לתנא דבי ר' ישמעאל, דלא מתרבי ראשו ארוך מכלל ופרט משום דלא דמי בכל צד, ואיצטריך "סלעם" יתירא לרבויי:
Rashi on Chullin 67a:5:1.english: "In the waters," "in the waters" twice - Since the two generalizations are adjacent [to one another], when you place the detail that follows them in between them, it is a [hermeneutical] rule in the Torah that you do not expound them as a generalization and a detail [kelal u'ferat], but rather as an amplification and a restriction [ribbui u'mi'ut] — for this is why the Merciful One separated the detail from the generalization, so that you should not expound it as a generalization and a detail. And the difference between ribbui u'mi'ut and kelal u'ferat is that when we expound [a verse as] a generalization and a detail, the detail serves as the definition of the generalization, and there is nothing in the generalization except what is [explicitly] in the detail — you may not include even something similar to it; and when [Scripture] states a second generalization for you after the detail, it serves to include something that is similar to the detail. However, when we expound [a verse as] an amplification and a restriction, the restriction does not define the amplification, but rather restricts [it] so that you do not infer everything from it, but only this [specific item] and things similar to it; thus, even without a second amplification we would include everything similar to the restriction, and the second amplification serves to include everything, while the restriction serves to exclude something that is not similar to it at all. And so we explain in the chapter Nigmar HaDin (Sanhedrin 45b) regarding [the Mishnah] "All who are stoned are hanged," that an amplification and restriction on its own brings in everything similar to it in any respect. And because it is expounded as an amplification and restriction, the first [mention of] "you may eat" is needed to permit [fish in] pits, which would otherwise come [under] the prohibition through [the rule of] amplification, restriction, and amplification; whereas if we expounded it as a generalization, detail, [and generalization], [fish in] pits would not have been included [in the prohibition], and the extra "you may eat" would not have been needed, for the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael holds that the first generalization is [to be taken] strictly [as limited by the detail], such that the final generalization includes only something similar to the detail in every respect — namely, flowing [waters]. And so too we said earlier regarding the generalization and detail of locusts according to the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael, that [a locust whose] head is elongated is not included by the generalization and detail because it is not similar [to the detail] in every respect, and the extra [mention of] sal'am was needed to include it.

Rashi on Chullin 67a:5:2.hebrew: ומאי מיעט מיעט בורות שיחין ומערות - אתאכלו יתירא סמיך, כדאמרי' במסקנא: א"כ תאכלו מאי אהני ליה:
Rashi on Chullin 67a:5:2.english: And what does it exclude? It excludes pits, ditches, and caves - It relies on the superfluous [word] "you may eat," as we say in the conclusion [of the passage]: "If so, what does [the word] 'you may eat' accomplish for him?"

Rashi on Chullin 67a:7:1.hebrew: ואיפוך אנא - דכיון דלאו טעמא יהיב למילתיה כשאר "כעין הפרט", אימא "תאכלו" למישרי חריצין, וריבויא לרבויי בורות:
Rashi on Chullin 67a:7:1.english: And let me reverse [it] - For since he did not give a reason for his statement, as [is done in] other [cases of] "like the specific example," say [that] "you may eat" [comes] to permit trenches, and the inclusive term [comes] to include pits [for prohibition]:

Rashi on Chullin 67a:7:2.hebrew: שהן עצורין - שאין להם מוצא ומבוא, אלא עצורין ככלים, ולא דמו לאיסורא במידי, דהא "ימים ונחלים" כתיב:
Rashi on Chullin 67a:7:2.english: Which are contained - For they have no outlet or inlet; rather, they are contained like vessels, and they do not resemble [what is] prohibited in any way, for "seas and streams" is written [in the verse]:

Rashi on Chullin 67a:8:1.hebrew: הי סתום והי מפורש - דאמרי' לעיל, "הואיל והתיר בסתום והתיר במפורש":
Rashi on Chullin 67a:8:1.english: Which is implicit and which is explicit - [referring to] that which we said above, "Since [Scripture] permitted [it] in the implicit [verse] and permitted [it] in the explicit [verse]":

Rashi on Chullin 67a:8:2.hebrew: יש לו מפורש - בההוא קרא דמשתעי ביש לו סנפיר וקשקשת, קרי מפורש להתיר כלים בלא סימני טהרה, כדדריש לעיל: "ימים ונחלים" הוא ד"אותם תאכלו", ולא אחרים; הא בכלים, אפי' אין לו תאכלו:
Rashi on Chullin 67a:8:2.english: "[Whatever] has [fins and scales]" is the explicit [source] - [He] calls that verse which speaks of "[whatever] has fins and scales" the explicit [source] for permitting [creatures in] vessels without signs of purity, as [the baraita] expounds above: [Only those in] "seas and rivers" [is where] "you may eat them," and not others; thus, [those] in vessels, even [when they] do not have [fins and scales], you may eat:

Rashi on Chullin 67a:9:1.hebrew: מיניה הוא דקא מישתרו כלים - כדפרישית, דקאי אמיעוט ד"אותם", דממעט אין לו גבי ימים ונחלים, כדכתיב: "ובנחלים אותם תאכלו", ולא שאין לו, וממילא דבכלים לא אימעיט. אבל קראי דמישתעי באין לו — דאמרן לעיל נמי דמישתרו מיניה, כדאמרן: "כל אשר אין לו בימים ובנחלים לא תאכלו", הא בכלים תאכלו — לא הוי מפורש להיתר כלים כולי האי, משום דאזהרת "לא תאכלו" לא סמיכא לפרטא אלא לכלל, ד"כל נפש החיה אשר במים לא תאכלו", ומשמע טפי דבכל מימות שבעולם, אפי' בכלים, אזהר. אלא אנן הוא דדרשינן ליה בכלל ופרט וכלל, דבדידיה נמי איכא ב' כללות סמוכין זה לזה אחר הפרט, דכתיב: "בימים ובנחלים מכל שרץ המים ומכל נפש החיה" וגו':
Rashi on Chullin 67a:9:1.english: It is from it that [fish in] vessels are permitted - As I explained [above], [this] refers to the exclusion of "them," which excludes [creatures] that do not have [fins and scales] regarding seas and rivers, as it is written: "and in the rivers, them you may eat," [meaning, them] and not [those] that do not have [fins and scales]; and consequently, [such creatures] in vessels are not excluded. However, the verses that speak of [creatures] that do not have [fins and scales] — from which we also said above that they are permitted, as we said: "all that have not [fins and scales] in the seas and in the rivers ... you shall not eat," [implying:] but in vessels you may eat — are not explicit regarding the permissibility of [fish in] vessels to that extent, because the prohibition "you shall not eat" is not juxtaposed to the specification ["in the seas and in the rivers"], but rather to the generalization, [as it states:] "all living creatures that are in the waters ... you shall not eat," which implies more [readily] that in all waters in the world, even in vessels, it prohibits [them]. Rather, it is we who expound it via [the principle of] a generalization, a specification, and a generalization, since in [that passage] too there are two generalizations juxtaposed to one another after the specification, as it is written: "in the seas and in the rivers, of all that swarms in the waters, and of all the living creatures," etc.:

Tosafot on Chullin 67a:5:1.hebrew: במים במים שני פעמים אין זה כלל ופרט אלא ריבה ומיעט - פי' בקונטרס: משום דברבוי ומיעוט מדריש, איצטריך "תאכלו" קמא למישרי בורות שיחין ומערות דאתו ברבוי ומיעוט ורבוי דאסור; דאילו כלל ופרט דרשינן, לא הוה מתרבי בורות, ולא איצטריך "תאכלו" יתירא, דקסבר תנא דבי ר' ישמעאל כללא קמא דוקא, ולא מרבינן בכלל בתרא אלא מידי דדמי ליה בכל צד לפרט, דהיינו נובעין. וצריך לומר דסוגיא דלעיל, דדריש כלל ופרט וכלל ואפ"ה איצטריך ליה ל"תאכלו" להתיר בורות שיחין ומערות, קסבר כללא בתרא דוקא, והוו מתרבו בורות שיחין ומערות אע"ג דלא דמו אלא בחד צד, שהם מים הגדלים על גבי קרקע. וכי פריך: "אי מה הפרט מפורש מים הגדלים על גבי קרקע ורבי אפילו בורות שיחין ומערות לאיסורא", הוה מצי לשנויי: קסבר כללא קמא דוקא ובעי' עד דדמי ליה בכל צד; אלא האמת קמתרץ, דמ"תאכלו" קדריש להו לעיל בברייתא. והשתא לפירוש זה לא פליגי מידי בהך מלתא סוגיא דלעיל ותנא דבי ר' ישמעאל דהכא. ויש לתמוה: דכי פריך בסמוך "ואיפוך אנא", ומשני "מרבה אני בורות שיחין ומערות להתירא שהם עצורין ככלים", למה לי להזכיר כלל "עצורין"? דהוה ליה למימר דאיבעי ליה לרבויי חריצין ונעיצין טפי לאיסורא לפי שהם נובעים כימים וכנחלים! לכך נראה דהנך חריצין ונעיצין דהכא איירי באין נובעין, ולהכי פריך: כיון דאין נובעין, מה לי בורות שיחין ומערות, מה לי חריצין ונעיצין? ומשני דחריצין ונעיצין, אע"ג שאין נובעין, דמו טפי לימים ונחלים שאין עצורים ככלים; אבל בורות שיחין ומערות עצורים ככלים, ולהכי סברא להתירא. והשתא, למאן דדריש ריבה ומיעט, מרבה חריצין ונעיצין שאין נובעין לאיסורא, והתירא ד"תאכלו" מוקי לה בבורות שיחין ומערות; אבל למאן דדריש לעיל כללי ופרטי, מרבה מ"תאכלו" להתירא אפי' חריצין ונעיצין שאין עצורים ככלים, כיון דאינן נובעים:
Tosafot on Chullin 67a:5:1.english: “In the waters,” “in the waters” twice is not a generalization and a detail, but rather an amplification and a restriction - Rashi explained: Because [the Tanna] expounds [the verse] as an amplification and a restriction, the first [instance of] “may you eat” is needed to permit pits, ditches, and caves, which would have been included [for prohibition] through [the rule of] amplification, restriction, and amplification; whereas if we were to expound [it] as a generalization and a detail, pits would not have been included, and the extra “may you eat” would not have been needed, because the Tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael holds that the first generalization is primary, and we do not include in the latter generalization anything except what is similar to the detail in every respect — namely, flowing [water]. And one must say that the sugya above, which expounds [it as] a generalization, a detail, and a generalization and even so needs “may you eat” to permit pits, ditches, and caves, holds that the latter generalization is primary, and [thus] pits, ditches, and caves would have been included even though they are only similar in one respect, in that they are water that grows on the ground. And when [the Gemara above] asks: “If [so], just as the detail is explicitly water that grows on the ground, [so too all water that grows on the ground,] and include even pits, ditches, and caves for prohibition,” it could have answered: [the Tanna] holds that the first generalization is primary, and we require [an item] to be similar to [the detail] in every respect; however, it gives the true answer, that [the Tanna] expounds them [as permitted] from “may you eat” above in the baraita. And now, according to this explanation, the sugya above and the Tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael here do not disagree at all in this matter. However, one may wonder: when [the Gemara] asks immediately below, “And let me reverse [it],” and answers, “I include pits, ditches, and caves for permission because they are enclosed like vessels,” why did it need to mention “enclosed” at all? For it should have said that it is more fitting to include trenches and water channels for prohibition because they are flowing like seas and like rivers! Therefore, it appears that these trenches and water channels here are dealing with [cases where they are] not flowing; and that is why [the Gemara] asks: since they are not flowing, what difference is there between pits, ditches, and caves, and trenches and water channels? And [the Gemara] answers that trenches and water channels, even though they are not flowing, are more similar to seas and rivers in that they are not enclosed like vessels; whereas pits, ditches, and caves are enclosed like vessels, and therefore it is logical [to include them] for permission. And now, according to the one who expounds [using] amplification and restriction, he includes trenches and water channels that are not flowing for prohibition, and he establishes the permission of “may you eat” as referring to pits, ditches, and caves; whereas according to the one who expounds above [using] generalizations and details, he includes from “may you eat” for permission even trenches and water channels that are not enclosed like vessels, since they are not flowing:
